newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi's SABIC signs agreement for $850 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's SABIC signs agreement for $850 mln loan.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said on Wednesday it had signed an agreement securing a $850 million syndicated loan for one of its affiliates.

"SABIC...had signed an agreement with a consortium of local, regional and international banks to secure a $850 million term loan to part-finance the construction of Arabian Industrial Fibers Company (Ibn Rushd) in Yanbu," a SABIC statement said.
SABIC said in November it had mandated local, regional and international banks to help finance petrochemical projects in Ibn Rushd, which is 47.96 percent owned by SABIC.

It named the banks as Saudi Arabia's Riyad Bank, Arab National Bank -- partly owned by Jordan's Arab Bank -- Arab Petroleum Investment Corp, Barclays Bank Plc, Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank, Industrial Bank of Japan, JP Morgan and Saudi Cairo Bank.

"We are pleased that the national, regional and international banks have come forward to fund this project which is expected to contribute immensely to industrial diversification and national development," SABIC's vice-chairman Ibrahim bin Salameh said.

Ibn Rushd would use the loan to finance the construction of a 350,000 tonnes per year purified terephthalic acid (PTA) plant, an aromatic plant which would produce 350,000 tonnes of benzene and 300,000 metric tonnes of paraxylene a year.
It would also produce orthoxylene and metaxylene.

SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, accounts for around five percent of the world's petrochemical production. It has embarked on a programme to raise its annual capacity to 28 million tonnes by the year 2000 from 23 million tonnes now.
